I love the idea. This would be very useful in sidebars as well as self posts.

Expandos work by making an AJAX request to load the content, which is not already in the page. So for images/videos for example, the image is only loaded when you click the expando button. For self-posts, it’s less obvious, but you are also making an AJAX request to load the post’s text content, which is not already loaded when you are viewing a list of posts on your frontpage or on a sub.

So this would not work with the expando mechanism, because any text you input via Markdown into the sidebar, would already exist inline in the page, in between other text that we don’t want to hide.

You don’t have to use :hover. If you prefer to expand on click, you can use :focus and :active.

I would do it something like this (not tested, writing this offhand):

Markdown:

- Every post must be related to [anime *An animated work produced and aired in Japan.*](#expand). Unrelated posts will be removed.

CSS:

li a[href="#expand"] {
 /* inline-block,
 padding on the right,
 background image for the icon */
}
li a[href="#expand"] em {
 display: none;
}
li a[href="#expand"]:focus em, li a[href="#expando"]:active em {
 display: block;
}

The entire link including the “icon” will be clickable, just like expandos. You can style it as an inline box that appears with the flow of the sidebar, or as a pseudo-popup/tooltip. You can even add CSS transitions if you want the fancy sliding box like expandos. Let me know if you need a full working example.
